version.changelog: L7b quality fix - VAGUE_TASK cleared, input/output sections added

llm.summary: The skill is a coherent SQL helper, but it enables broad command-line database execution and write/delete-style operations without clear safeguards for real databases.

dimensions.detail: Use of read/write/exec and database CLIs is proportionate for a command-line SQL skill, but those permissions become high impact when pointed at production databases.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The inspected artifact is a single Markdown skill file with no bundled executable scripts or installer behavior.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Activation guidance is broad for database operations and data storage management, with no default read-only posture, production/test distinction, or explicit confirmation requirement before mutating data.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill discusses persistent database writes, batch scripts, PRAGMA changes, and transactions, but does not clearly require user authorization, backups, rollback planning, or environment scoping before changes.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is SQL querying and execution, and the capability set matches that purpose, but it explicitly covers create/query/modify/delete operations and includes account-balance UPDATE examples, which can affect persistent business data.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with an agent using command-line database tools. Treat it as capable of changing real database state; prefer read-only credentials, test databases, explicit per-command approval, backups, and transactions with rollback plans before allowing writes or deletes.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] unexpected: The broad activation language is artifact-backed and materially relevant because the skill also advertises write and exec authority for database work.
[SQP-2] expected: Create, modify, delete, write, and exec capabilities are expected for an SQL execution skill, but the artifact under-discloses the risk of persistent data modification.
[SQP-2] expected: The transaction example is purpose-aligned SQL guidance, but using account-balance UPDATE statements without a warning or confirmation guidance supports the Review concern.
